sections.h2: What the Northampton Register of Deeds does
sections.html:
The office holds the county's permanent records: land instruments, plats, UCC filings and vital records. Sellers meet it because the deed to the buyer, and the security for the buyer's loan, are filed here.

Land books begin in 1741, marriage entries in 1863, and birth and death entries in December 1913. Older entries are found through paper indexes. Staff also issue marriage licenses and certified vital records, so say up front that you are calling about a deed.

Phone 252-534-2511 with questions, and ask there for the street address, hours and holiday closings.

A free search is available at northamptonrod.org. The computerized index starts January 1, 1991, and it was the first time these records appeared on the internet.

  • From 1991 forward, search the website for deeds, deeds of trust and releases.
  • For older records, plan on the hard-copy indexes at the office.
  • Search under the owner's name exactly as the latest recorded deed spells it, because the index follows document names.

The title history of a family farm or inherited lot may begin before 1991. If your parcel passed through several generations, phone the office before assuming the website shows everything.

The county is sparsely populated: an estimated 16,491 people on 536.70 square miles of land in mid-2025, which is 5.6 percent fewer than in 2020. Of 7,857 households, 74.6 percent own, and the middle owner-occupied home is valued around $114,500. Rents sit near $758. Builders took out 15 permits in 2025.

For a long-held house, a clean recorded chain of title matters most, and a gap in the index is easier to fix before a buyer's title search finds it. Modest values and a shrinking population also mean that an inherited or repair-heavy house can take a while to sell on the open market. A cash sale closes quickly and skips lender inspections and appraisals, which suits some owners of that kind of property.

Fees are uniform statewide, so Northampton charges what neighboring counties charge. G.S. 161-10 is the legal basis, calling the fees complete and exclusive and collectible before filing.

sections.h2: Who covers the deed tax at a sale?
sections.html:
The seller. Each deed carries a tax of $1 per $500 of consideration, with a leftover under $500 counted as a full $500, and G.S. 105-228.30 makes the transferor deliver it to the register ahead of filing. The county general fund keeps half. The other half goes to the state revenue department in a monthly remittance.

The office page also links a Deed Tax Certification form, a deed of trust fee change notice and a public records redaction request. Ask which, if any, your closing needs.

sections.h2: Other filings that touch a sale
sections.html:
The office also files loan security instruments, releases and plats. Satisfactions cost nothing, so an old paid-off loan can be released for free, and the buyer's lender will expect that.

  • A plat is $21 a sheet, which applies if a lot is split before sale.
  • A nonstandard document adds $25.
  • Assignments add $10 for each extra index reference, and a party beyond the twentieth adds $2 a name.
  • A UCC record runs $38 for one or two pages.

Owners of several parcels, or of older estate property, can ask the office to look through the index for liens, releases and earlier deeds ahead of closing. Anything older than 1991 requires a phone call.

A sale touches the register, the tax department and, with an estate, the clerk of court. Work through this list before closing.

  • Locate the latest recorded deed and compare its names to the people signing.
  • Search 1991 forward for any deed of trust never released, and call about older ones.
  • Ask the tax department what is owed for every open year, including bills from earlier years.
  • Download the parcel's property tax card and GIS map from the tax page so the acreage and description agree with the deed.
  • After an owner's death, confirm with the clerk of court who may sign and whether a will has been probated.

The tax page also links a room occupancy tax return, so if a lodging operator runs out of the property, ask the tax department about closing that account.

Send every filing with a self-addressed stamped envelope, the signed deed and payment.

  • Compare the deed against the recording standards published by the state association of registers.
  • Enclose the filing fee and the seller's deed tax.
  • Phone to learn whether mail, couriers or drop-off are accepted.
  • Keep the confirmation, because under G.S. 47-18 a deed binds creditors and later buyers only after it is registered.

Filing order sets priority, so a deed that arrives late can rank behind an earlier lien. In a typical sale the closing attorney handles all of this, and the seller's job is to sign, supply the payoff letters and ask for a recorded copy afterward.

sections.h2: Timeline from signing to recorded deed
sections.html:
Think of the recording as the last step of a short chain. Before closing, your attorney or title firm gathers the deed, the payoff for any old loan, and proof that property taxes are handled. At closing you sign, and the seller's deed tax is collected with the fee. The deed then goes to the register, and the date it is registered is the date that counts against anyone else claiming the house. Afterward the office indexes it, and from 1991 forward you can find it on the free website under the owner's name.

If a buyer is paying cash, there is no lender waiting on a new deed of trust, so the packet is smaller and the filing is simpler. Whatever the route, ask for the recording date in writing and keep it with your sale papers.

The Tax Department, at 126 E. Jefferson St. in Jackson, bills Northampton parcels. Bills for 2026 are due September 1, 2026, and interest holds off until after January 5, 2027. Numbers: 252-534-4461 (main), 252-534-5941 (land records) and 252-534-3431 (listing).

The tax page links appeal forms and a list of county property for sale. Before fixing a closing date, ask what balance clears the parcel. An owner who prefers no repairs or showings can ask Cash Home Buyers for a cash offer and set it beside the payoff and recording costs.

faqs.q: Which office records deeds for Northampton parcels?
faqs.a: The Northampton County Register of Deeds. A deed takes effect against creditors and later buyers once registered in the county where the parcel lies, under G.S. 47-18. Phone 252-534-2511 for the street address and hours.

faqs.q: What is the filing fee for a deed here?
faqs.a: A deed runs $26 for the first 15 pages with $4 added per extra page, and a deed of trust is $64 for 35 pages with the same $4 add-on. The seller's deed tax, $1 per $500 of price, is a separate payment.

faqs.q: Is there a free online index?
faqs.a: Yes, from 1991 forward at northamptonrod.org. Older records are searched in paper indexes at the office.

faqs.q: Is the seller or buyer responsible for deed tax?
faqs.a: The seller. G.S. 105-228.30 puts the payment on the transferor, due at the register of deeds before filing, at $1 per $500 of consideration.

faqs.q: When is the property tax deadline?
faqs.a: September 1. Interest on 2026 bills starts only after January 5, 2027. State law then adds 2 percent through January and 0.75 percent per month afterward.
